actors.threat_actor: NastyShrew (Gamaredon, UAC-0010, Primitive Bear, Aqua Blizzard)
actors.notes: Russia-nexus, one of the most active and persistent Russian threats. Champion Social Engineering [#9] — high-frequency phishing with .lnk/.ps1 files. High Malware [#7] — Pteranodon VBScript chains, multi-stage payloads. High Function Abuse [#1] — dead drop resolvers on paste sites (teletype.in, rentry.co), geofenced C2 infrastructure, LotL techniques. VPS purchased with cryptocurrency, strict Ukrainian IP geofencing. Members arrested in Thailand (Phuket) in Feb/Nov 2025.

Russia-nexus, first publicly attributed by Dutch intelligence May 2025. Champion Social Engineering [#9] — event-driven tactical targeting aligned with NATO summits, EU Defense meetings, Brussels Indo-Pacific Forum, SIDEC, World Agriculture Forum. High Identity Theft [#4] — credential theft via software brand impersonation (Microsoft, ESET). High Malware [#7] — PLUGGYAPE backdoor. Rapid infrastructure rotation — purchases domains and hosting from multiple providers, anticipates disruption.

Russia-nexus, specialized reconnaissance unit. Champion Social Engineering [#9] — impersonation of Kropyva (Ukrainian artillery guidance), Delta, Teneta, Diia, e-Cherha apps. High Identity Theft [#4] — Signal device-linking credential theft via custom phish kit. High Function Abuse [#1] — PINPOINT (JS geolocation via browser API), MESHAGENT (legitimate RMM for persistence). Geolocation capability suggests overlap with kinetic targeting.

actors.threat_actor: ClumsyToad (Mustang Panda, Earth Preta, BASIN, Twill Typhoon)
actors.notes: China-nexus, high-frequency regional espionage. Champion Malware [#7] — PlugX/Korplug, Toneshell, Yokai, PUBLOAD, SnakeDisk USB worm, DLL side-loading. High Physical Attack [#8] — SnakeDisk propagates via USB removable drives (geofenced to Thailand). High Social Engineering [#9] — spear-phishing with localized lures. Moderate Client Exploit [#3] — shifted from .lnk to .msc (Windows Management Console) files to bypass EDR. Cloudforce One disrupted 20+ accounts, 400+ domains, 87 core assets.

China-nexus, edge network appliance exploitation specialist. Champion Server Exploit [#2] — F5 BIG-IP, VMware vCenter, VMware ESXi. Champion Malware [#7] — BRICKSTORM (Go-based ELF, Garble-obfuscated), GarbTerm; reverse C2 logic (malware as web server, C2 connects via wss://); masquerades as VMware/Postgres processes. High Function Abuse [#1] — DNS over HTTP (DoH) for C2 resolution, proxy tunneling. Maintained F5 access for >1 year, exfiltrated source code and undisclosed vulnerability documentation.

actors.threat_actor: FrumpyToad (APT41, Wicked Panda, Brass Typhoon, BARIUM)
actors.notes: China-nexus, dual espionage + financial motivation. Champion Function Abuse [#1] — weaponized Google Calendar for cloud-to-cloud C2 (TOUGHPROGRESS reads/writes encrypted commands in event descriptions), LotX operations. Champion Malware [#7] — TOUGHPROGRESS, KEYPLUG, ShadowPad, DUSTTRAP, DUSTPAN. High Supply Chain [#10] — known for software supply chain attacks. High Social Engineering [#9] — spear-phishing via serverless platform redirect chains. High Identity Theft [#4] — credential stealers. Delivery chain uses compromised government sites for payload hosting.

North Korea-nexus, Lazarus subcluster. High Supply Chain [#10] — XenoRAT payloads hosted on Google Drive and Dropbox, GitHub for covert C2. High Malware [#7] — XenoRAT. High Function Abuse [#1] — leverages high-reputation cloud providers (Google Drive, Dropbox, GitHub) to blend into legitimate enterprise traffic and bypass security filters. Analytical parasitism on legitimate platforms.

North Korea-nexus, Lazarus subcluster. Contagious Interview campaign — social engineering via fake job interviews targeting crypto developers (ClickFix technique). Champion Malware [#7] — custom implants. High Social Engineering [#9] — fake job interviews, dev recruitment lures. High Identity Theft [#4] — credential harvesting. High Supply Chain [#10] — software supply chain compromise. Targets cryptocurrency sector for regime revenue generation.

North Korea-nexus, industrialized IT worker infiltration. Champion Social Engineering [#9] — deepfake video interviews, fabricated LinkedIn/GitHub personas, rented US citizen credentials, laptop farm residency illusion. Champion Function Abuse [#1] — legitimate corporate system access used for intelligence collection and revenue funneling. High Identity Theft [#4] — uses legitimately-issued credentials obtained through identity fraud. No traditional malware — operates entirely through designed system capabilities. Detection: impossible travel alerts, mouse-jiggling software, deepfake video micro-artifacts.

Iran-nexus. High Social Engineering [#9] — spear-phishing targeting government and private sectors. High Malware [#7] — custom backdoors and implants. Moderate Server Exploit [#2] — targets telecommunications infrastructure. High Function Abuse [#1] — post-compromise lateral movement. Targets Middle East (Israel, Saudi Arabia, UAE) and Southern Europe for espionage and regional influence.

Unsophisticated individual actor demonstrating the MOE paradigm. Champion Function Abuse [#1] — automated secret scanning (TruffleHog) for credential discovery, AI-assisted SaaS navigation using LLMs in real time to navigate Salesforce. High Identity Theft [#4] — uses harvested credentials to authenticate to SaaS integrations. No traditional exploitation or malware — operates entirely through legitimate tools and designed functionality. Breached hundreds of corporate Salesforce tenants through the Salesloft/Drift integration. Demonstrates that unsophisticated actors can now execute high-impact breaches through industrialized credential discovery and AI navigation.

Botnet operators behind record-breaking DDoS attacks. Champion Flooding [#6] — 31.4 Tbps UDP flood (November 2025), 19 world records in 2025, attacks peak in seconds and end within 10 minutes. Champion Malware [#7] — botnet malware controlling estimated 1-4 million infected hosts, residential proxy tunneling. Moderate Server Exploit [#2] — IoT device exploitation for botnet recruitment. Moderate Identity Theft [#4] — credential stuffing at industrial scale (94% of login attempts from bots). Kimwolf is the successor network; 550+ C2 nodes null-routed in early 2026.
